name: Gmail (Google Workspace APIs)
summary: Creating the Google Cloud OAuth client takes minutes, but reading or modifying Gmail uses restricted scopes: you need brand verification, data-access verification and an annual third-party security assessment (CASA) before the general public can connect. Until then you are capped at 100 test users whose authorisations expire every 7 days.
difficulty_reason: Restricted-scope verification involves a demo video, policy review and a paid annual CASA security assessment; Google says verification can take several months.

effort.hands_on: 1-2 h for the client; 1-3 days to prepare verification materials; CASA remediation varies
effort.first_connection: Same day (as a listed test user)
effort.production: Several weeks to several months (Google: 'can take several months')
effort.waiting_on: Brand verification (often minutes), data-access verification of each restricted scope, then the CASA assessment with an empanelled assessor - repeated annually.

bottom_line: Start verification the week you start building, because it is the critical path. First check whether you truly need to read mail: gmail.send (sensitive) and gmail.labels (non-sensitive) avoid the CASA assessment, but note that gmail.metadata, gmail.compose, gmail.readonly and gmail.modify are all restricted. Use a separate Cloud project for dev/test (exempt, 100 users) and a production project you submit. Get a verified domain, a homepage that is not just a login page, and a privacy policy that discloses Google user data use - on the same domain - before you submit.
app_type: Google Cloud project + OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform: Branding, Audience, Data access) + OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application).

scope_paths.name: Read, draft or modify mail - even headers only (typical agent)
scope_paths.review: Restricted-scope verification + annual CASA security assessment

scope_paths.name: Internal tool for one Workspace org
scope_paths.review: None - set user type to Internal (project must belong to that org)

prerequisites.item: Google Cloud project (separate dev and prod)
prerequisites.detail: Dev/test projects are exempt from verification but capped at 100 users.
Every authorised domain on the consent screen must be verified by a project owner/editor.

prerequisites.item: Public homepage on the verified domain
prerequisites.detail: Must describe the app, not be only a login page, and link to the privacy policy.

prerequisites.item: Privacy policy on the same domain
prerequisites.detail: Must disclose how you use Google user data and match the link on the consent screen.
Shows the full OAuth flow, consent screen in English with exact scopes, and each feature that uses each scope.
Restricted scopes require an annual assessment by a Google-empanelled assessor; cost depends on assessor and tier.

stages.name: Set up for development
stages.goal: You and up to 100 test users can connect.

steps.title: Create a dev project and configure Google Auth Platform
steps.detail: Branding (app name, support email), Audience (External, Testing), Data access (add Gmail scopes).

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API and create a Web OAuth client
steps.detail: APIs & Services > Library > Gmail API; Clients > Create client > Web application; add redirect URIs.

steps.title: Add test users
steps.detail: Audience > Test users (max 100). They'll see an unverified-app warning.

steps.title: Implement OAuth with offline access
steps.detail: access_type=offline, prompt=consent for a refresh token; handle invalid_grant (expiry, revocation, password change for Gmail scopes).

stages.name: Prepare production verification
stages.goal: A production project ready to submit.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest scopes and write justifications
steps.detail: Agent maps features to scopes and drafts why narrower scopes won't work (required by reviewers).

steps.title: Verify domains in Search Console
steps.detail: DNS TXT record; agent can generate the record, you apply it.

steps.title: Publish homepage and privacy policy
steps.detail: Agent drafts the Google user data disclosure (incl. Limited Use and any AI-training statement); you review and publish.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Agent writes the shot list; you record the end-to-end flow with the exact scopes visible.

stages.name: Get verified
stages.goal: Production users can connect without the 100-user cap or warning screen.

steps.title: Brand verification
steps.detail: Usually completes in minutes; ambiguous cases get manual review. Results valid 7 days if you don't publish.

steps.title: Data-access (restricted scope) verification
steps.detail: Respond quickly to reviewer emails sent to the project contacts.

steps.title: CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Work with an empanelled assessor; fix findings; repeat annually.

token_facts.value: Expire after 7 days unless only openid/email/profile are requested

token_facts.fact: Refresh tokens per Google Account per client

token_facts.value: Revoked when the user changes their password

gotchas.title: 7-day expiry in Testing
gotchas.detail: Agents that 'stop working after a week' during pilots are hitting the Testing-status expiry, not a bug.

gotchas.title: 100-user cap
gotchas.detail: Unverified apps with sensitive/restricted scopes are limited to 100 new users; the cap lifts only after verification.

gotchas.title: Scopes in code must match the consent screen
gotchas.detail: Requesting a scope not configured on the consent screen triggers the unverified-app screen even after verification.

gotchas.title: AI training disclosure
gotchas.detail: If you use data for model training, the demo video must show explicit user consent for it.

gotchas.title: Annual re-assessment
gotchas.detail: Restricted-scope apps must re-verify every year; missing it risks losing access.

blockers.cause: Unverified sensitive/restricted scopes, or code requests a scope not on the consent screen.
blockers.next_step: Align scopes; submit for verification; meanwhile add pilot users as test users.
Move to production + verification, or re-consent weekly during the pilot.

blockers.cause: User type is Internal and user is outside the org.
blockers.next_step: Switch to External (triggers verification) or use a per-customer internal deployment.

blockers.cause: Reviewer believes a narrower scope works.
blockers.next_step: Show in the video exactly which feature needs the scope, or switch to the narrower scope.

agent_can: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes for your features (and flag which ones trigger CASA)
Draft scope justifications and the privacy-policy Google-data section
Generate the DNS TXT record and consent-screen values
Implement OAuth with refresh, invalid_grant handling and the 100-token-per-user limit
Pre-check your homepage/privacy policy against Google's brand requirements
you_must: Own the Google Cloud project and Search Console domain verification
Record and upload the demo video
Contract and pay a CASA assessor; remediate findings

claims.claim: Restricted scopes require an annual security assessment by a Google-empanelled assessor; sensitive scopes do not.
Testing status: up to 100 test users; their authorisations (and refresh tokens) expire after 7 days unless only basic profile scopes are requested.
Unverified apps are limited to 100 new users after the unverified-app screen; verification 'can take several months'.
Internal (same Workspace org), personal (<100 users), dev/test and service-owned-data apps do not need verification.
Brand verification usually completes in a few minutes; compliant results valid 7 days.
Limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per client ID; the oldest is invalidated without warning.
Unknown client_id produces an invalid_client 'The OAuth client was not found' error page.
claims.note: Probe returned 302 to /signin/oauth/error with an encoded invalid_client message.

claims.claim: Google's OIDC discovery advertises PKCE S256/plain and the device-code grant.
gmail.send is sensitive and gmail.labels non-sensitive; gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose and gmail.metadata are restricted.
claims.note: Checked 2026-11-04. Corrected an earlier draft that implied gmail.metadata was a lighter option - it is restricted.

open_questions: Typical CASA cost and duration vary by assessor and tier - get quotes early.
Actual verification duration is not published as an SLA; plan for weeks, not days.
Not tested end-to-end (requires a Google Cloud account and a submitted app).
